input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: Argument.get_help_record returns self.help unchanged, so the second element of the tuple is None for an undocumented argument even though format_arguments now feeds every record straight into formatter.write_dl without a fallback.
- failure path: A command declares two arguments and sets help on only one; running it with --help makes write_dl measure and wrap a None description and the help command crashes with a TypeError instead of printing usage.

Reviewer finding
- description: get_help_record now returns (metavar, self.help) without falling back to an empty string. When help is None, the tuple's second element is None instead of the empty description the docstring promises.
- rationale: Trigger: a command with at least one Argument that has help and another Argument without help, then --help is run. format_help_text calls write_dl with a (metavar, None) row, and write_dl or its text wrapping fails on the None. Result: a crash, typically a TypeError, instead of rendering the help. The old code used the `or (metavar, "")` fallback and the new code drops it. It should be `self.help or ""`.
critique: The finding names the same defect: get_help_record returns None as the help element when help is unset, and write_dl crashes with a TypeError when a command has one documented and one undocumented argument. It says format_help_text calls write_dl instead of format_arguments, but the faulty operation and the failure path are the same.
